claims.text: The initial material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Sc or Y is a low-density refractory alloying element.
Adding Sc or Y to HfMoTaTiZr will reduce its density.
Adding Sc or Y will preserve the room-temperature mechanical performance of HfMoTaTiZr.
Adding Sc or Y will preserve the high-temperature mechanical performance of HfMoTaTiZr.
Sc or Y addition will refine the alloy's grain structure.
Sc or Y will form a solid solution with the existing alloy elements.
Grain refinement and solid-solution strengthening will maintain the alloy's strength.
The modified alloy will have a density below 10.0 g cm−3.
The modified alloy will have a room-temperature yield strength above 1600 MPa.
The modified alloy will have a yield strength above 800 MPa at 1000 °C.
The modified alloy will maintain or improve fracture toughness.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has an elevated-temperature yield strength of 855 MPa.
The proposed performance boundary extends from room temperature to 1600 °C.

contradictions.description: The predicted strength targets are above 1600 MPa at room temperature and above 800 MPa at 1000 °C, whereas the falsification rule accepts lower values of 1500 MPa and 750 MPa, so the rejection criteria do not directly test the stated prediction.

A density below 10.0 g cm−3 is presented as the predicted outcome, but a 5% reduction from the 10.21 g cm−3 baseline requires density at or below approximately 9.70 g cm−3; thus some outcomes satisfying the prediction would fail the experiment's density criterion.
The stated boundary extends to 1600 °C, but mechanical testing and quantitative rejection criteria are provided only for room temperature and 1000 °C.
The requested single intervention is not uniquely specified: Sc and Y are alternative additions, and their concentrations are also left variable.
